games.title: Medical Physiology Ii: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which segment of the small intestine has the highest density of villi and is primarily responsible for nutrient absorption?
questions.explanation: The jejunum has the greatest villous surface area for absorption.

questions.q: What is the primary hormone that stimulates gastric acid secretion by parietal cells?
questions.explanation: Gastrin directly stimulates parietal cells to secrete H⁺.

questions.q: Which enzyme, secreted by the pancreas, is essential for the digestion of carbohydrates in the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic amylase hydrolyzes starches into maltose and dextrins.

questions.q: The hormone secretin is released in response to which of the following?
options: Low luminal pH in the duodenum
High luminal pH in the duodenum
High luminal calcium in the duodenum
High luminal bile salts in the duodenum
questions.explanation: Secretin is secreted when duodenal pH falls below 4.5, stimulating bicarbonate secretion.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of bile salt reabsorption in the ileum?
questions.explanation: Bile salts are actively transported by the apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter (ASBT).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the gallbladder?
questions.explanation: Bile salts are synthesized in the liver, not the gallbladder.

questions.q: The hormone motilin is released during which phase of the interdigestive migrating motor complex?
questions.explanation: Motilin peaks during phase III, triggering a strong contraction.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains the mechanism of action of the drug sucralfate in peptic ulcer disease?
options: Binds to ulcer base forming a protective barrier
questions.explanation: Sucralfate forms a viscous, adherent complex that shields the ulcer.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most common cause of chronic pancreatitis in the United States?
questions.explanation: Alcohol abuse is the leading cause of chronic pancreatitis.

questions.q: Which of the following hormones is released by the enteroendocrine cells of the duodenum in response to fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Cholecystokinin is secreted in response to fat and stimulates gallbladder contraction.

games.title: Acute and chronic pancreatitis: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most common cause of acute pancreatitis in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Gallstones account for ~40–50% of acute pancreatitis cases in the UK.

questions.q: A 52‑year‑old man presents with epigastric pain radiating to the back, elevated serum amylase and lipase, and a CT scan showing peripancreatic fat stranding. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
questions.explanation: Early aggressive IV fluids are critical in acute pancreatitis to prevent hypovolemia and organ failure.

questions.q: Which imaging modality is most sensitive for detecting chronic pancreatitis in a patient with recurrent abdominal pain?
questions.explanation: EUS is the most sensitive for early chronic pancreatitis, detecting parenchymal changes and ductal abnormalities.

questions.q: A patient with chronic pancreatitis develops painless jaundice. The most likely explanation is:
questions.explanation: Chronic pancreatitis can cause a pancreatic duct stricture that compresses the common bile duct, leading to painless jaundice.

questions.q: Which laboratory finding is most characteristic of acute pancreatitis?
questions.explanation: Serum amylase (and lipase) are markedly elevated in acute pancreatitis.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old woman with chronic pancreatitis has a serum amylase of 120 U/L (normal 30–110 U/L). Which of the following is most likely?
questions.explanation: A mildly raised amylase in chronic pancreatitis reflects low‑grade inflammation, not an acute flare.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major risk factor for the development of pancreatic cancer in patients with chronic pancreatitis?
questions.explanation: Smoking is the strongest independent risk factor for pancreatic cancer in chronic pancreatitis.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most appropriate long‑term management for a patient with chronic pancreatitis who is malnourished and has exocrine insufficiency?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy corrects exocrine insufficiency and improves nutrition.

questions.q: In acute pancreatitis, the Ranson criteria are most useful for:
questions.explanation: Ranson criteria are used to predict the severity and mortality risk of acute pancreatitis.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the pathophysiology of chronic pancreatitis?
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes ductal obstruction, leading to inflammation, fibrosis, and chronic pancreatitis.

games.title: TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENES & CELL CYCLE CONTROL: case showdown
games.topic: TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENES & CELL CYCLE CONTROL
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old woman presents with a painless, firm mass in the left breast. Mammography shows a spiculated lesion and core needle biopsy reveals invasive ductal carcinoma with loss of heterozygosity at the TP53 locus. What is the most likely tumor suppressor gene involved?
questions.explanation: Loss of TP53 is common in invasive ductal carcinoma and is a key tumor suppressor in breast cancer.

questions.q: A 28‑year‑old man is diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a t(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation. Which tumor suppressor pathway is most likely disrupted?
questions.explanation: t(8;21) involves RUNX1‑RUNX1T1 fusion, which interferes with p53-mediated apoptosis.

questions.q: A 60‑year‑old man has a 2‑cm ulcerated lesion on the scalp. Histology shows squamous cell carcinoma with loss of CDKN2A (p16) expression. Which cell cycle regulator is directly affected?
questions.explanation: CDKN2A encodes p16, an inhibitor of CDK4/6; its loss leads to unchecked CDK4/6 activity.

questions.q: A 35‑year‑old woman presents with a rapidly enlarging cervical lymph node. Fine‑needle aspiration shows metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation. Which tumor suppressor gene is most likely inactivated in this tumor?
questions.explanation: Melanoma frequently inactivates CDKN2A (p16), leading to CDK4/6 activation.

questions.q: A 50‑year‑old man has a 3‑cm mass in the left kidney. Imaging and biopsy reveal clear cell renal cell carcinoma with loss of VHL gene function. Which pathway is dysregulated as a result?
questions.explanation: VHL loss leads to stabilization of HIF‑1α and upregulation of VEGF, driving angiogenesis.

questions.q: A 22‑year‑old woman presents with a painless, firm mass in the left ovary. Histology shows granulosa cell tumor with FOXL2 C134W mutation. Which tumor suppressor pathway is most likely compromised?
questions.explanation: FOXL2 mutation is associated with loss of p53 pathway activity in granulosa cell tumors.

questions.q: A 65‑year‑old man has a 4‑cm ulcerated lesion on the lower lip. Histology shows squamous cell carcinoma with loss of p53 immunoreactivity. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: B) Wide local excision with 2‑cm margin
questions.explanation: Mohs surgery provides tissue-sparing, margin-controlled excision ideal for lip SCC.

questions.q: A 30‑year‑old woman presents with a 2‑cm breast mass. Core needle biopsy shows ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) with loss of BRCA1 expression. Which of the following best describes the role of BRCA1 in cell cycle control?
options: B) Promotes DNA repair via homologous recombination
questions.explanation: BRCA1 is essential for homologous recombination DNA repair, a key tumor suppressor function.

games.title: Intestinal Stomas: Colostomy and Ileostomy, Types, Care and: case showdown
games.topic: Intestinal Stomas: Colostomy and Ileostomy, Types, Care and
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 68‑year‑old man presents with a 2‑day history of abdominal pain and distension after a recent laparotomy for sigmoid volvulus. On examination the abdomen is tense and the surgical wound shows a well‑healed colostomy site. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Stomal obstruction is common after colostomy and presents with abdominal distension and pain.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old woman with ulcerative colitis develops a 3‑day history of fever, abdominal pain, and a new opening of the ileostomy with purulent drainage. What is the next best step?
options: B. Perform a CT scan of the abdomen
C. Obtain a stool culture and start IV antibiotics
questions.explanation: Purulent drainage suggests infection; obtain culture and start IV antibiotics.

questions.q: A 30‑year‑old man with a loop ileostomy for Crohn’s disease presents with a 1‑day history of abdominal pain and a 2‑cm protrusion of the stoma. Which type of stoma complication is most likely?
questions.explanation: A protrusion of the stoma indicates prolapse.

questions.q: A 55‑year‑old woman with a permanent colostomy for diverticular disease reports a sudden change in stool output to watery, foul‑smelling stools. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.explanation: Watery, foul stools indicate overflow from the proximal colon.

questions.q: A 70‑year‑old man with a permanent ileostomy for colorectal cancer has a 2‑day history of abdominal pain, fever, and a tender, erythematous stoma. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Tender, erythematous stoma with fever suggests infection.

questions.q: A 60‑year‑old woman with a loop colostomy for Hirschsprung disease has a 1‑day history of abdominal distension and a firm, non‑tender abdomen. The stoma is functioning normally. What is the next best step?
options: B. Order a CT scan of the abdomen
C. Obtain a plain abdominal X‑ray
questions.explanation: Plain X‑ray can identify obstruction proximal to the stoma.

questions.q: A 50‑year‑old man with a permanent ileostomy for ulcerative colitis presents with a 2‑day history of abdominal pain and a 1‑cm ulcerated area on the stoma. What is the most appropriate management?
options: A. Apply a stoma patch and observe
D. Apply a stoma dressing and start topical steroids
questions.explanation: An ulcerated stoma requires topical steroids and dressing to promote healing.

questions.q: A 65‑year‑old woman with a loop colostomy for colorectal cancer has a 3‑day history of abdominal pain, nausea, and a 1‑cm defect in the stoma. What is the most likely complication?
questions.explanation: A defect in the stoma indicates necrosis of the stoma tissue.

games.title: Weeks 6 & 7 Must-Know: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which class of drug is used as the first-line treatment for acute asthma exacerbations in the emergency department?
questions.explanation: Short‑acting β₂‑agonists (e.g., salbutamol) are the first‑line bronchodilator for acute asthma.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of amiodarone?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone primarily blocks potassium channels (Class III antiarrhythmic), prolonging the action potential duration and refractory period.

questions.q: Which drug is most commonly associated with the characteristic side effect of blue‑tinged urine?
questions.explanation: Rifampicin produces a characteristic red‑orange discoloration of urine and other body fluids.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old patient is started on a drug that inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme, leading to increased plasma levels of a concurrent oral contraceptive. Which drug is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Ketoconazole is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, raising levels of drugs metabolised by this enzyme.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main indication for the use of enoxaparin?
options: A. Primary prevention of deep vein thrombosis in orthopedic surgery
B. Treatment of acute pulmonary embolism
C. Management of chronic heart failure
D. Antiplatelet therapy in acute coronary syndrome
questions.explanation: Enoxaparin, a low‑molecular‑weight heparin, is indicated for treatment of acute pulmonary embolism.

questions.q: Which drug is known to cause a characteristic ‘blue‑ish’ discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone can produce a slate‑blue discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes, a classic adverse effect.

questions.q: What is the primary therapeutic target of the drug lisinopril?
questions.explanation: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor, blocking conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common side effect of high‑dose corticosteroids used in asthma?
questions.explanation: High‑dose corticosteroids can cause hyperglycaemia due to increased gluconeogenesis.
